1.e4 e5 2.Bc4 b5 3.Bxb5.strategy: Accepts the gambit pawn instead of retreating. White is a pawn up and can step the bishop back to safety when it is attacked, so Black has to show real compensation in open lines and a quick centre.

1.e4 e5 2.Bc4 b5 3.Bxb5 c6.strategy: Hits the bishop and prepares to build a pawn centre, the point of the gambit. But the bishop simply retreats with the pawn still White's, and Black has to prove the compensation: playable, though pleasant for White.
1.e4 e5 2.Bc4 b5 3.Bxb5 c6.name: Bishop's Opening: Anderssen Gambit
1.e4 e5 2.Bc4 b5 3.Bxb5 c6.background: Adolf Anderssen played both this move and 3...f5 after 3.Bxb5.

1.e4 e5 2.Bc4 b5 3.Bxb5 f5.strategy: Strikes at e4 with a pawn but weakens the king's diagonal and stays a pawn down. After 4.d4, taking on e4 loses at once: Qh5+ g6 Qxe5+ checks the king and wins the rook on h8.
1.e4 e5 2.Bc4 b5 3.Bxb5 f5.name: Bishop's Opening: Thorold Gambit
1.e4 e5 2.Bc4 b5 3.Bxb5 f5.background: Adolf Anderssen played both this move and 3...c6 after 3.Bxb5.
